pliosaurus:enwiki:5.title: Pliosaurus (Later discoveries and other species, part 2)

pliosaurus:enwiki:6.title: Pliosaurus (Later discoveries and other species, part 3)

facts.statement: Pliosaurus fossils date from the Late Jurassic to the Lower Cretaceous, specifically from the Kimmeridgian to the Valanginian stages, with a possible record from the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic to Lower Cretaceous (Kimmeridgian to Valanginian), Possible Oxfordian record

facts.statement: The genus Pliosaurus was formally described by Richard Owen in 1841.
facts.quote: authority: Owen, 1841

facts.statement: Although mentioned in 1824, Pliosaurus was not formally described until 1841 by Richard Owen, who first placed it in Plesiosaurus before elevating it to its own genus later that year.
facts.quote: Although initially mentioned in a 1824 paper by William Daniel Conybeare, it was not until 1841 that it was first formally described by Richard Owen as belonging to a new species of Plesiosaurus, before being given its own genus by the same author later that year.

facts.statement: The name Pliosaurus means "more lizard" because the animal's appearance was considered more reminiscent of crocodilians than of other plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: The genus name Pliosaurus means "more lizard", Owen naming the taxon of because its appearance being more reminiscent of crocodilians than to Plesiosaurus.

facts.statement: Since a 2013 paper, only six species of Pliosaurus are firmly recognized as valid.
facts.quote: only six are firmly recognised as valid since a 2013 paper.

facts.statement: The second known specimen of P. funkei was famously nicknamed "Predator X" before its formal description.
facts.quote: the most famous being "Predator X", used to refer to the second known specimen of P. funkei.

facts.statement: A large specimen consisting only of cervical vertebrae found in Abingdon is estimated to have exceeded 11 meters in length if fully grown.
facts.quote: a large specimen composed entirely of cervical vertebrae discovered in Abingdon and putatively assigned to the genus could have reached a length exceeding 11 m.

facts.statement: The skulls of the largest known Pliosaurus species exceed 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: The elongated skull of Pliosaurus is robust, and those of the largest known species exceed 2 m in length.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus teeth are robust and have a trihedral cross-section, which is a main diagnostic trait of the genus.
facts.quote: The teeth are also robust and are trihedral in cross-section, which is one of the main diagnostic traits of the genus.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus has a relatively short neck with only 18 cervical vertebrae compared to other plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: The neck is one of the most recognizable features of the taxon, being relatively short compared to other plesiosaurs, having only 18 cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: The limbs of Pliosaurus were modified into flippers, with the front flippers of P. funkei reaching up to 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: The limbs of Pliosaurus were modified into flippers, with the anterior flippers of P. funkei reaching up to 3 m in length.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus skulls were reinforced to withstand the stresses of feeding.
facts.quote: Pliosaurid skulls are reinforced to better withstand the stresses of their feeding.

facts.statement: The rostrum of some Pliosaurus species likely contained a neurovascular system capable of detecting prey movements in the water.
facts.quote: The rostrum of some species contains internal structures that likely housed a neurovascular system capable of detecting the movements of nearby prey in the water.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus was adapted to aquatic life, swimming using a method known as subaqueous flight.
facts.quote: Pliosaurus was well-adapted to aquatic life, using its flippers for a method of swimming known as subaqueous flight.

facts.statement: In 1824, William Daniel Conybeare established the species Plesiosaurus giganteus for plesiosaur specimens with shortened cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: In 1824, William Daniel Conybeare established a new species of the genus Plesiosaurus, Plesiosaurus giganteus, to include all plesiosaurian specimens with shortened cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: The Market Rasen specimen is now stored in the Oxford University Museum of Natural History under the catalog number OUMNH J.9245.
facts.quote: This specimen has since been stored in the Oxford University Museum of Natural History, where it has since been catalogued as OUMNH J.9245.

facts.statement: In 1841, Richard Owen described the jaw anatomy of the Market Rasen specimen.
facts.quote: In 1841, Richard Owen described the anatomy of the jaws of the Market Rasen specimen.

facts.statement: The specific name brachydeirus is derived from Ancient Greek words meaning "short" and "neck" or "throat," referring to the animal's short neck.
facts.quote: The specific name brachydeirus also comes from Ancient Greek and comes from the words βραχύς (brakhús, "short"), and δειρή (deirḗ, "neck" or "throat"), in reference to its cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: In 1869, Richard Owen erroneously claimed that P. grandis was the type species of Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1869, the same author erroneously claimed that another species formerly attributed to Pliosaurus, P. grandis, would be the type species of this genus.

facts.statement: In 1871, John Phillips corrected Owen's errors by recognizing P. brachydeirus as the type species and using the spelling Pleiosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1871, John Phillips corrected most of Owen's taxonomic errors, recognizing P. brachydeirus as the type species and using the original spelling Pleiosaurus.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic studies place Pliosaurus in a derived position within Thalassophonea, often showing it is related to Gallardosaurus.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic classifications place Pliosaurus in a relatively derived position within the Thalassophonea, with the genus often being recovered as related to Gallardosaurus.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus lived from the Upper Jurassic to the Lower Cretaceous in what is now Europe and South America.
facts.quote: It lived from the Upper Jurassic to the Lower Cretaceous in what is now Europe and South America.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus used its long, robust snouts to capture large prey, piercing them with trihedral teeth located at the back of the jaws.
facts.quote: The long, robust snouts of the various Pliosaurus species were used to capture large prey, piercing them with the numerous trihedral teeth at the back of the jaws.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus shared its habitat with invertebrates, fish, thalattosuchians, ichthyosaurs, and other plesiosaurs, all of which served as prey.
facts.quote: The fossil record shows that Pliosaurus shared its habitat with a variety of other animals, including invertebrates, fish, thalattosuchians, ichthyosaurs, and other plesiosaurs, which would undoubtedly have constituted prey for the larger species.

facts.statement: Nestor Novozhilov named P. rossicus in 1948 based on partial fossils found in mines in the Lower Volga Basin, Russia.
facts.quote: In 1948, Nestor Novozhilov named the species P. rossicus on the basis of two more or less partial specimens discovered in two mines in the Lower Volga Basin in Russia

facts.statement: A second, larger specimen of P. rossicus, catalogued as PIN 2440/1, was discovered as a complete skeleton in May 1945.
facts.quote: The second specimen, more imposing and since catalogued as PIN 2440/1, was discovered in May 1945 as a complete skeleton

facts.statement: P. funkei was described in 2012 by Knutsen and colleagues from two large specimens found in the Svalbard archipelago, Norway.
facts.quote: The species P. funkei was described in 2012 by Knutsen and colleagues based on two large specimens discovered in the Norwegian archipelago of Svalbard

facts.statement: Fossils of P. funkei were collected at 2 km intervals over eight seasons between 2004 and 2012 by Jørn Hurum in the southern Sassenfjorden.
facts.quote: The fossils were collected at 2 km (1.25 mi) intervals during eight seasons of fieldwork conducted from 2004 to 2012 by Jørn Hurum in the southern Sassenfjorden

facts.statement: Due to their remarkable size, the teams nicknamed the holotype of P. funkei "The Monster" and the referred specimen "Predator X".
facts.quote: The rather remarkable size of the fossils led the Hurum's paleontological teams to nickname them "The Monster" for the holotype and "Predator X" for the referred specimen

facts.statement: P. funkei gained media attention leading to its appearance in a 2009 History Channel documentary and a 2010 science fiction horror film.
facts.quote: This popularity led the species to appear in a 2009 documentary broadcast on the American television channel History, then in a 2010 low-budget science fiction horror film

facts.statement: Knutsen and colleagues suggest that P. funkei and P. rossicus might represent different growth stages of the same species, though they maintain them as distinct taxa.
facts.quote: In their article, Knutsen and colleagues conclude that it cannot be definitively excluded that P. funkei and P. rossicus would represent different ontogenetic stages of the same species based on the available material

facts.statement: Roger B. J. Benson and colleagues described three new Pliosaurus species in 2013, all based on fossils found in England.
facts.quote: In a 2013 paper published in the mega journal PLOS ONE, Roger B. J. Benson and colleagues described three additional species of Pliosaurus, all of whose fossils were discovered in England

facts.statement: P. kevani was described with a holotype consisting of a large, nearly complete adult skull found in a cliff at Osmington Mills Bay, Dorset.
facts.quote: The first of these three species described was P. kevani, whose holotype consists of a large, nearly complete skull of a probable adult, which was discovered in a cliff at Osmington Mills Bay, Dorset

facts.statement: The holotype skull of P. kevani was collected over eight years from fragments weighing up to 60 kg.
facts.quote: This specimen was collected over a period of eight years via fragmented parts weighing up to 60 kg

facts.statement: The name P. kevani honors Kevan Sheehan, a cafe owner who collected most of the holotype skull during his daily walks along the shore.
facts.quote: The specific name for this taxon honours Kevan Sheehan, owner of a small cafe overlooking the sea at Osmington Mills, who collected most of the holotype specimen during daily walks along the shore

facts.statement: P. westburyensis and P. carpenteri were described in 2013, with holotypes discovered in a quarry near Westbury, Wiltshire.
facts.quote: The other two species described in the 2013 paper are P. westburyensis and P. carpenteri, both of whose holotypes were discovered in a quarry near Westbury, Wiltshire

facts.statement: The holotype of P. westburyensis (a skull with postcranial remains) was found on July 2, 1980, while the holotype of P. carpenteri (a partial skeleton) was found on May 12, 1994.
facts.quote: The holotype of the first species consists of a skull with some postcranial remains, while the second consists of a partial skeleton, respectively discovered on July 2, 1980, and May 12, 1994

facts.statement: Benson and colleagues argue that the differences between P. westburyensis and P. carpenteri are significant enough to warrant separate species status.
facts.quote: However, in the article published the following year, Benson and his colleagues consider that the differences between them are relatively significant when observed in the context of specimens from other localities, and therefore justify a specific distinction

facts.statement: The holotype of P. carpenteri, nicknamed "Doris", was temporarily mounted for a special exhibition at the Bristol Museum & Art Gallery from June 2017 to February 2018.
facts.quote: From June 2017 to February 2018, the holotype specimen of P. carpenteri, then nicknamed "Doris", was temporarily mounted as part of a special exhibition at Bristol Museum & Art Gallery

facts.statement: Two South American species of Pliosaurus, P. patagonicus and P. almanzaensis, were described in 2014 and 2018 from fossils found in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: The South American species P. patagonicus and P. almanzaensis were described in 2014 and 2018, respectively, from fossils discovered in different localities of Neuquén Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. patagonicus is a partial skull discovered in 1975 by Zulma Gasparini and a team from the La Plata Museum in the Zapala Department.
facts.quote: The holotype of P. patagonicus consists of a partial skull discovered in 1975 by Zulma Gasparini and a team from the La Plata Museum, in the Zapala Department.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. patagonicus, catalogued as MLP 80-V-29-1, was incorrectly prepared using acid, which damaged the palate and other cranial bones.
facts.quote: The specimen, since catalogued as MLP 80-V-29-1 within the museum, was prepared using acid, a technique frequently employed at the time, but its application was incorrect.

facts.statement: The taxonomic identity of the P. patagonicus holotype remained uncertain for over three decades due to damage from incorrect preparation.
facts.quote: As a result, the taxonomic identity of the specimen remained uncertain for more than three decades.

facts.statement: Before being identified as P. patagonicus, the holotype was assigned to Stretosaurus sp., Liopleurodon cf. macromerus, and Liopleurodon sp. between 1982 and 2011.
facts.quote: Thus, in works led by Gasparini, the specimen was first assigned to Stretosaurus sp. from 1982 to 1992, then referred to as Liopleurodon cf. macromerus in 1997, before being classified simply as Liopleurodon sp. from 2007 to 2011.

facts.statement: Gasparini and José P. O'Gorman reidentified the damaged holotype as P. patagonicus after a new preparation, with the name referring to Patagonia.
facts.quote: A new preparation of the specimen allowed Gasparini and José P. O'Gorman to reidentify it as a new species of the genus Pliosaurus, P. patagonicus, the specific epithet referring to Patagonia, the region where the holotype was discovered.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. almanzaensis includes a large skull, several vertebrae, and flipper skeletal elements.
facts.quote: The holotype of P. almanzaensis consists of a large, relatively well-preserved skull followed by several vertebrae and skeletal elements from the flippers.

facts.statement: P. almanzaensis was discovered in 1986 by brothers Sergio and Rafael Cocca in Cajón de Almanza, about 10 km east of Loncopué.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 1986 by brothers Sergio and Rafael Cocca in the locality of Cajón de Almanza (hence the name), about 10 km east of the village of Loncopué.

facts.statement: The entire P. almanzaensis specimen was collected in February 1987 and catalogued as MOZ 3728P, with its stratigraphic position determined by Luis A. Spalletti in January 1988.
facts.quote: In February 1987, the entire specimen, later catalogued as MOZ 3728P within the museum, was finally collected, and Luis A. Spalletti precisely determined its stratigraphic position in January 1988.

facts.statement: P. almanzaensis was formally described in 2018 by O'Gorman, Gasparini, and Spalletti as a new species contemporaneous with P. patagonicus.
facts.quote: However, the specimen was only formally described in 2018 by O'Gorman, Gasparini, and Spalletti as representing a new species of Pliosaurus, contemporaneous with P. patagonicus.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus belongs to the large-headed, short-necked "pliosauromorph" morphotype, unlike the small-headed, long-necked "plesiosauromorph" morphotype.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurs are usually categorized as belonging to the small-headed, long-necked "plesiosauromorph" morphotype or the large-headed, short-necked "pliosauromorph" morphotype, Pliosaurus belonging to the latter category.

facts.statement: Before formal description, media estimates suggested P. funkei reached 13 to 15 meters and the P. kevani holotype reached 12 to 16 meters.
facts.quote: Even before their fossils were formally described in the scientific literature, the media estimated their lengths as ranging from 13 to 15 m for the P. funkei specimens and from 12 to 16 m for the holotype of P. kevani.

facts.statement: Comparisons with other pliosaurid genera led to a body length estimate of 9.8 to 14.4 meters for the large Pliosaurus sp. specimen.
facts.quote: Based on comparisons made with other pliosaurid genera, the authors gave a body length estimate of 9.8 to 14.4 m.

facts.statement: In 2026, Ruizhe Jackevan Zhao concluded that P. cf. kevani and P. funkei are similar in size, with an estimated body length of 9.8 meters and mass of 10.7 to 10.9 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2026, Ruizhe Jackevan Zhao compared the specimens attributed to P. cf. kevani and P. funkei, and concluded that both would not be significantly different in terms of measurements, with an estimated body length of 9.8 m and body mass of approximately 10.7 – 10.9 t.

facts.statement: P. kevani is the only recognized Pliosaurus species with sub-trihedral teeth, featuring slightly flattened labial surfaces and finely distributed enamel ridges.
facts.quote: However, P. kevani is the only recognized species in which the teeth are sub-trihedral in shape, possessing slightly flattened labial surfaces with finely distributed enamel ridges.

facts.statement: In P. kevani and P. carpenteri, premaxillary teeth vary in size (anisodont), whereas in P. brachydeirus and P. westburyensis, they do not.
facts.quote: In some species such as P. kevani and P. carpenteri, the premaxillary teeth are anisodont, meaning they vary in size, which is not the case in P. brachydeirus or P. westburyensis.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus species can be distinguished by the number of teeth in the premaxillae, maxillae, mandibular symphysis, and dentary.
facts.quote: The different species of Pliosaurus can also be distinguished by the number of teeth present in the premaxillae, maxillae (the latter two sometimes bearing caniniform dentition), the mandibular symphysis, and the dentary as a whole.

facts.statement: Dental counts for some Pliosaurus species remain uncertain due to poor fossil preservation, though known counts vary significantly between species like P. brachydeirus, P. rossicus, P. funkei, P. kevani, P. westburyensis, and P. carpenteri.
facts.quote: However, since not all fossils are sufficiently well preserved, the dental counts of some species remain uncertain: P. brachydeirus possessed four to six premaxillary teeth, twenty-two or more maxillary teeth, thirty-five to thirty-seven dentary teeth, and more than seven to thirteen pairs of symphyseal teeth; P. rossicus had six premaxillary teeth and six pairs of symphyseal teeth; P. funkei had at least five premaxillary teeth and six pairs of symphyseal teeth; P. kevani had six premaxillary teeth, about twenty-five maxillary teeth, more than twenty-eight to thirty-seven dentary teeth, and more than six to fifteen pairs of symphyseal teeth; P. westburyensis had more than five premaxillary teeth, about twenty-five maxillary teeth, more than twenty-one dentary teeth, and possibly nine pairs of symphyseal teeth; and P. carpenteri had six premaxillary teeth, more than twenty-seven maxillary teeth, twenty-seven dentary teeth, and eight to nine pairs of symphyseal teeth.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus had massive, short cervical vertebrae with flattened, subcircular to oval centers.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae of Pliosaurus are massive, short, and possess flattened centra that are subcircular to slightly oval in shape.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus likely had double-headed cervical ribs, a trait shared with other Jurassic pliosaurids.
facts.quote: Like other pliosaurids that lived during the Jurassic, Pliosaurus likely possessed double-headed cervical ribs.

facts.statement: P. funkei had exceptionally long forelimbs that could reach up to 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Limb proportions also vary between species. For example, P. funkei is distinguished by particularly elongated forelimbs, which could reach up to 3 m

facts.statement: The finger bones (phalanges) of Pliosaurus were hourglass-shaped, getting shorter and narrower toward the tips.
facts.quote: The phalanges are hourglass-shaped, becoming shorter and narrower distally.

facts.statement: Halstead (then Tarlo) performed the first major revision of the Pliosaurus genus in 1960.
facts.quote: In 1960, Halstead (then called Tarlo) revised the taxonomy of Late Jurassic pliosaurids, making the first revision of the type genus.

facts.statement: A comprehensive taxonomic revision of the entire Pliosaurus genus was published by Knutsen in 2012 alongside the official description of P. funkei.
facts.quote: Simultaneously with the publication of the official description of P. funkei in 2012, Another article written by Knutsen alone and concerning the taxonomic revision of the genus Pliosaurus as a whole is published.

facts.statement: Benson and colleagues identified six valid species of Pliosaurus in 2013: P. brachydeirus, P. rossicus, P. funkei, P. kevani, P. westburyensis, and P. carpenteri.
facts.quote: In 2013, Benson and colleagues recognised the validity of the following six species: P. brachydeirus, P. rossicus, P. funkei, P. kevani, P. westburyensis, and P. carpenteri.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley established the family Pliosauridae in 1874 to include animals similar to Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1874, Harry Govier Seeley named a new family of plesiosaurs, Pliosauridae, to contain forms similar to Pliosaurus.

facts.statement: Benson and colleagues proposed in 2012 that Pliosauridae is closely related to Plesiosauroidea, forming a clade called Neoplesiosauria.
facts.quote: In 2012, Benson and colleagues recovered a different topology, with Pliosauridae being more closely related to Plesiosauroidea than Rhomaleosauridae. This pliosaurid-plesiosauroid clade was termed Neoplesiosauria.

facts.statement: Benson and Druckenmiller defined the clade Thalassophonea in 2013 to include short-necked pliosaurids while excluding earlier, long-necked forms.
facts.quote: In 2013, Benson and Druckenmiller named a new clade within Pliosauridae, Thalassophonea. This clade included the "classic", short-necked pliosaurids while excluding the earlier, long-necked, more gracile forms.

facts.statement: Fischer and colleagues (2023) placed P. almanzaensis within Pliosaurus but assigned P. patagonicus to the Cretaceous subgroup Brachaucheninae.
facts.quote: In 2023, Valentin Fischer and colleagues recovered P. almanzaensis within the genus in their cladograms, but placed P. patagonicus among the Brachaucheninae, a subgroup of thalassophoneans whose representatives mainly lived during the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The exact evolutionary relationship between pliosaurids and other plesiosaurs remains uncertain.
facts.quote: Exactly how pliosaurids are related to other plesiosaurs is uncertain.

facts.statement: Scientists debated whether pliosaurids were closer to Elasmosauridae or Polycotylidae in the 1940s, with arguments based on shoulder anatomy versus skull and neck features.
facts.quote: In 1940, palaeontologist Theodore E. White considered pliosaurids to be close relatives of Elasmosauridae based on shoulder anatomy. However, in 1943, Samuel P. Welles thought that pliosaurids were more similar to Polycotylidae, as they both had large skulls and short necks, among other characteristics.

facts.statement: Smith and Dyke (2008) hypothesized that Pliosaurus is the closest relative of Peloneustes.
facts.quote: In 2008, Adam S. Smith and Gareth J. Dyke considered Pliosaurus to be the sister taxon of Peloneustes.

facts.statement: It is debated whether P. patagonicus and P. almanzaensis should be included in the genus Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: The inclusion of the species P. patagonicus and P. almanzaensis within the genus Pliosaurus has been discussed by some authors.

facts.statement: P. kevani is notable for having a large postcranial skeleton, which is rare for the genus.
facts.quote: A possible exception is P. kevani, one of whose referred specimens consists of a large postcranial skeleton.

facts.statement: The coracoid bone of P. funkei is one of the largest found in any pliosaurid.
facts.quote: The coracoid of P. funkei is among the largest identified in pliosaurids.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurs likely maintained a constant body temperature, possibly through endothermy, similar to birds.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurs were well-adapted to marine life. They grew at rates comparable to those of birds and had high metabolisms, indicating homeothermy or even endothermy.

facts.statement: A 2019 study suggests Plesiosaurs had enlarged red blood cells that aided them during diving.
facts.quote: A 2019 study by palaeontologist Corinna Fleischle and colleagues found that plesiosaurs had enlarged red blood cells, based on the morphology of their vascular canals, which would have aided them while diving.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus swam using a method called subaqueous flight, utilizing its flippers as hydrofoils.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurs such as Pliosaurus employed a method of swimming known as subaqueous flight, using their flippers as hydrofoils.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurs were unique among marine reptiles for using all four limbs for propulsion while keeping their vertebral column still.
facts.quote: Plesiosaurs are unusual among marine reptiles in that they used all four of their limbs, but not movements of the vertebral column, for propulsion.

facts.statement: A 2022 computer model found that Plesiosaurs produced more drag than similarly sized cetaceans or ichthyosaurs due to their large flippers.
facts.quote: Computer modelling by Susana Gutarra and colleagues in 2022 found that due to their large flippers, a plesiosaur would have produced more drag than a comparably-sized cetacean or ichthyosaur.

facts.statement: In 1988, Judy Massare proposed that Plesiosaurs could actively hunt prey rather than waiting, due to their body shape reducing drag.
facts.quote: Due to the reduction in drag by their shorter, deeper bodies, Judy Massare proposed in 1988 that plesiosaurs could actively search for and pursue their food instead of having to lie in wait for it.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus was a top marine predator with an exceptionally strong bite, though its skull was weak against twisting forces.
facts.quote: Pliosaurus is interpreted by palaeontologists as a marine predator at the top of the food chain, with powerful cranial musculature that gave it an exceptionally strong bite, although its skull was relatively weak against twisting or lateral bending.

facts.statement: Unlike relatives adapted to small prey, Pliosaurus favored a strategy of short, targeted bites to the back of the jaw where pressure was greatest.
facts.quote: Unlike basal thalassophoneans such as Peloneustes and Luskhan, which were better adapted to small, mobile prey, Pliosaurus appeared to favor a predatory strategy based on short, targeted bites, delivered to the back of the jaw where the force of pressure was greatest.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus exerted a bite force of 9,600 to 48,000 newtons, comparable to or greater than the largest living crocodilians.
facts.quote: By modeling the mandibular musculature and reconstructing the geometry of the skull using computed tomography and finite element analysis techniques, the researchers determined that the force exerted ranged from 9,600 to 48,000 newtons depending on the area of the lower jaws, a force comparable to, or even greater than, that of the largest living crocodilians.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus likely ate a wide variety of prey, from fish to smaller marine reptiles, immobilizing them before crushing or dismembering them.
facts.quote: It likely captured a wide variety of marine prey, ranging from medium-sized fish to smaller marine reptiles, which it subdued by firmly immobilizing with its robust jaws before crushing or swallowing them in dismemberment.

facts.statement: In 2015, researchers suggested a Pliosaurus-like animal inflicted bite marks on an indeterminate ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur.
facts.quote: A Pliosaurus-like pliosaur has also been suggested to have inflicted bite marks upon an indeterminate ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur by Nikolay Zverkov and colleagues in 2015.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus is considered a visually oriented predator with greatly enlarged orbits indicating high visual acuity.
facts.quote: Pliosaurs are generally regarded as visually oriented predators. The cranial anatomy of the holotype specimen of P. westburyensis reveals greatly enlarged orbits, indicative of large eyes and suggesting a high degree of visual acuity.

facts.statement: Unlike modern whales, Plesiosaurs did not possess echolocation due to a lack of acoustic isolation in their auditory capsules.
facts.quote: In contrast, the lack of acoustic isolation in the auditory capsules indicates that, unlike modern cetaceans, pliosaurs did not possess echolocation.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurs had vision adapted for low-light conditions, such as in turbid coastal waters or deep photic zones.
facts.quote: The size and arrangement of the orbits further suggest that their vision was effective under low-light conditions, such as in the turbid waters of coastal seas or the deeper part of the photic zone.

facts.statement: Plesiosaurs had remarkably small nasal cavities that were likely used for sensory functions like aquatic olfaction rather than respiration.
facts.quote: The nasal cavities of Pliosaurus are remarkably small relative to the size of the skull, too reduced to provide effective respiration. This peculiarity has led to the hypothesis that these structures were not primarily involved in ventilation but instead had a sensory function.

facts.statement: The neurovascular canals in the P. kevani rostrum reached up to 23 mm in diameter, with finer branches about 2 mm wide.
facts.quote: The largest canals reach 23 mm in diameter, while the finest branches, about 2 mm wide, extend to the periphery of the rostrum.

facts.statement: A specimen of P. carpenteri showed advanced degeneration of the jaw joint that caused the lower jaw to misalign progressively.
facts.quote: Detailed observations revealed erosive osteoarthritis of the mandibular joint, particularly at the articular glenoid surfaces, which led to a progressive misalignment of the lower jaw

facts.statement: Pathological features in a P. carpenteri specimen included bone growth around tooth sockets and irregular cavities in the jawbone.
facts.quote: Among other anomalies observed in the specimen are the presence of callus-like bone growth around certain tooth alveoli and irregular lateral cavities in the mandible

facts.statement: Pathologies in a P. carpenteri specimen suggest the animal suffered from age-related disease and long-term mechanical issues like asymmetric biting.
facts.quote: Together, these pathological modifications indicate not only age-related degenerative disease, but also long-term mechanical consequences—such as asymmetric biting caused by the altered joint

facts.statement: Researchers debated whether an asymmetric ridge on the skull of P. westburyensis was a tumor or a variable trait possibly linked to sexual dimorphism, but this idea was later contradicted.
facts.quote: However, as similar structures have been observed in other pliosaurs, Sassoon and colleagues instead proposed that it represents a variable character, even suggesting the possibility of sexual dimorphism, in line with their interpretation of specimens BRSMG Cc332 and BRSMG Cc6172, although this latter view has since been contradicted by Benson et al. (2013)

facts.statement: A depression on the skull of P. kevani is interpreted as possibly being a bite mark, a disease, or a surface change from fossilization.
facts.quote: This feature could correspond to a pathology, a bite mark, or an alteration of the bone surface that occurred during the specimen's biostratinomic history

facts.statement: Several species of Pliosaurus lived during the Upper Jurassic in the Kimmeridge Clay Formation of England.
facts.quote: P. brachydeirus, P. kevani, P. westburyensis, P. carpenteri and a possible specimen of P. rossicus are known from the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages of the Upper Jurassic in the Kimmeridge Clay Formation, England

facts.statement: The environment where many Pliosaurus species lived was a deep-sea marine zone about 150 to 200 meters deep.
facts.quote: This formation was deposited in a deep-sea marine environment reaching about 150 to 200 m depth, known as the Jurassic Sub-Boreal Seaway

facts.statement: The first specimens of P. rossicus were found in Tithonian rocks in the Lower Volga Basin of Russia.
facts.quote: In Russia, the first two known specimens of P. rossicus were discovered in Tithonian rocks of the Lower Volga Basin

facts.statement: A tooth found on Mount Sheludivaya in Crimea was identified as Pliosaurus in 2015 based on its triangular shape.
facts.quote: In 2015, a single tooth discovered at the summit of Mount Sheludivaya in Crimea was attributed to Pliosaurus by Zverkov on the basis of the typical trihedral shape of the genus

facts.statement: The tooth from Crimea dates to the Early Cretaceous, marking the latest known record of the Pliosaurus genus.
facts.quote: Dating to the late Valanginian of the Early Cretaceous, it represents the most recent known occurrence of the genus in the fossil record

facts.statement: P. funkei fossils are found in Tithonian rocks in the Agardhfjellet Formation of Svalbard.
facts.quote: In Svalbard, P. funkei is known from Tithonian-aged rocks of the Slottsmøya Member of the Agardhfjellet Formation

facts.statement: The rocks containing P. funkei were deposited in a shallow water environment associated with methane seeps.
facts.quote: This unit consists of a mix of shales and siltstones and was deposited in a shallow water methane seep environment

facts.statement: Scientists believe sea ice was present in the waters where P. funkei lived during the winter due to the high latitude and cool climate.
facts.quote: Though direct evidence from Slottsmøya is currently lacking, the high latitude of this site and relatively cool global climate of the Tithonian mean that sea ice was likely present at least in the winter

facts.statement: As a top predator, P. funkei likely ate other marine reptiles found in its environment.
facts.quote: As a large apex predator, P. funkei may have included some of them in its diet

facts.statement: The genus Pliosaurus was named by Richard Owen in 1841.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Owen, 1841

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Pliosaurus is P. brachydeirus.
facts.quote: type_species: Pliosaurus brachydeirus

facts.statement: Known species of Pliosaurus include P. brachydeirus, P. carpenteri, P. funkei, P. macromerus, P. kevani, P. patagonicus, P. portentificus, P. rossicus, and P. westburyensis.
facts.quote: subdivision: P. brachydeirus Owen, 1840 P. carpenteri Benson et al., 2013 P. funkei Knutsen, Druckenmiller & Hurum, 2012 P. macromerus Philips, 1871 P. kevani Benson et al., 2013 P. patagonicus Gasparini & O'Gorman, 2014 P. portentificus Noè et al., 2004 P. rossicus Novozhilov, 1948 P. westburyensis Benson et al., 2013

facts.statement: Pliosaurus were giant predators that ate fish, squid, and other marine reptiles.
facts.quote: Eran gigantescos depredadores, que se alimentaban a base de peces, calamares, y otros reptiles marinos

facts.statement: Unlike other pliosaurs, Pliosaurus had teeth that were triangular in cross-section.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros pliosáuridos, Pliosaurus tenía dientes de aspecto triangular en corte transversal

facts.statement: Richard Owen named Pliosaurus because the type specimen's anatomy was more similar to crocodiles than to Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: Richard Owen describió el espécimen tipo de Pliosaurus brachydeirus, él mostró que las características anatómicas de este eran más cercanas a las de los cocodrilos que las que tenía Plesiosaurus

facts.statement: The type species Pliosaurus brachydeirus was discovered in southern England.
facts.quote: Los restos de Pliosaurus brachydeirus fueron descubiertos en el sur de Inglaterra, y constituye la especie tipo de Pliosaurus.

facts.statement: Richard Owen described the genus Pliosaurus in 1841.
facts.quote: Owen, al describir el género en 1841, comparó su constitución física con la de los típicos plesiosauros de cuello largo.

facts.statement: Owen described the species Pliosaurus brachyspondylus in 1839.
facts.quote: Owen describió a esta especie en 1839.

facts.statement: The species Pliosaurus rossicus is known from two specimens discovered in Chuvashia, Russia.
facts.quote: Pliosaurus rossicus es un pliosaurio relativamente pequeño conocido a partir de dos especímenes descubiertos en Chuvashia, Rusia.

facts.statement: The Natural History Museum of Oslo announced the discovery of a fossil possibly belonging to the genus Pliosaurus in March 2009.
facts.quote: En marzo de 2009 el Museo de Historia Natural de Oslo anunció el descubrimiento del fósil de una criatura posiblemente perteneciente al género Pliosaurus

facts.statement: Fossils of a Pliosaurus specimen estimated to have lived 147 million years ago are exhibited at the Natural History Museum of Oslo.
facts.quote: Los restos de la criatura, que vivió hace unos 147 millones de años, son exhibidos en el Museo de Historia Natural de Oslo.

facts.statement: Pliosaurus remains were discovered in permafrost in Svalbard, Norway, in June 2006 and excavated in mid-2008.
facts.quote: Los restos del depredador fueron descubiertos en el permafrost en Svalbard, Noruega, en junio de 2006, y finalmente excavados a mediados de 2008

facts.statement: The excavation team found 20,000 fragments of the creature's skeleton.
facts.quote: El equipo encontró 20.000 fragmentos del esqueleto de la criatura

facts.statement: The excavation was led by a Norwegian team headed by Jørn Hurum.
facts.quote: por un equipo noruego liderado por Jørn Hurum.

facts.statement: The name Pliosaurus brachydeirus means "short-necked".
facts.quote: El nombre de esta especie significa "de cuello corto".

facts.statement: The species name P. brachyspondylus means "short vertebra" because its first cervical vertebrae are shorter than the posterior ones.
facts.quote: su nombre de especie significa "vértebra corta", debido a que su principal característica es el hecho de que las primeras vértebras cervicales son más cortas que las posteriores.

facts.statement: The species name P. macromerus means "large femur".
facts.quote: Pliosaurus macromerus (que significa "fémur grande")

facts.statement: The jaw of the Svalbard specimen was over 3 meters long and could have exerted 10 times the pressure of any modern animal and 4 times that of Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Su mandíbula, de más de 3 metros de largo, puede haber ejercido más presión que la de cualquier otro animal conocido, 10 veces más que cualquier animal actual, e incluso 4 veces más que el de Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: The Svalbard specimen was estimated to have teeth longer than 30 centimeters.
facts.quote: poseía dientes de más de 30 cm de largo

facts.statement: Bone analysis suggests the animal swam using only its two front flippers, using the rear pair only for extra thrust when chasing prey.
facts.quote: Análisis de los huesos de las cuatro aletas sugieren que el animal nadaba usando solo sus dos aletas anteriores, usando el par posterior solo cuando necesitaba un empuje adicional para perseguir y capturar a sus presas.

facts.statement: The species Pliosaurus funkei was previously known by the nickname "Predator X".
facts.quote: La especie Pliosaurus funkei, fue conocida anteriormente con el sobrenombre de Depredador X

facts.statement: The Svalbard specimen was initially estimated to be over 15 meters long and weigh 45 tons, making it the largest predator in history.
facts.quote: que se estimó medía más de 15 metros, y pesaba una 45 toneladas, con lo que sería el mayor depredador de la historia

facts.statement: Further scrutiny of the Svalbard specimen fossils revised its estimated total length to a range of 10.0 to 12.8 meters.
facts.quote: El escrutinio de los fósiles del espécimen de Svalbard reveló que no era tan grande como se afirmó en un principio; la longitud total estimada se ha revisado llegando a un rango de 10.0 - 12.8 metros.

facts.statement: Based on the distribution pattern of pliosaurs, it is believed they had a cosmopolitan distribution, similar to modern whales.
facts.quote: Debido al patrón de distribución de los pliosaurios se cree que tenían distribución cosmopolita, como las ballenas actuales.

facts.statement: The validity of species such as P. brachydeirus, P. brachyspondylus, and P. macromerus depends on the author, though they are known from the Kimmeridgian of England.
facts.quote: La validez de las especies citadas a continuación depende de los autores: Pliosaurus brachydeirus, Pliosaurus brachyspondylus y Pliosaurus macromerus son conocidos del Kimmeridgiense de Inglaterra.

facts.statement: According to Knutsen (2012), there is no reason to classify Pliosaurus andrewsi within the genus Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: según Knutsen (2012) no hay razón para clasificarlo dentro del género Pliosaurus.

facts.statement: Knutsen (2012) provisionally retained P. rossicus as a separate species but noted that further examination is needed to determine if it is a distinct taxon or a junior synonym of P. macromerus.
facts.quote: Knutsen (2012) lo retuvo provisionalmente como una especie separada, pero subrayó que se necesitan exámenes adicionales para determinar si P. rossicus es ciertamente un taxón separado o meramente un sinónimo más moderno de Pliosaurus macromerus.

facts.statement: Knutsen (2012) provisionally retained P. rossicus as a separate species.
facts.quote: Knutsen (2012) lo retuvo provisionalmente como una especie separada

facts.statement: P. rossicus was later made the type species of the genus Strongylokroptaphus, assigned to the genus Liopleurodon, and then reassigned to the genus Pliosaurus by Knutsen (2012).
facts.quote: y fue más adelante convertida en la especie tipo del género Strongylokroptaphus, y posteriormente asignado al género Liopleurodon antes de ser nuevamente asignado al género Pliosaurus por Knutsen (2012).

facts.statement: P. portentificus is considered a nomen dubium by Knutsen (2012).
facts.quote: Pliosaurus portentificus procede de finales del Kimmeridgiense de Inglaterra. Es considerado por Knutsen (2012) como un nomen dubium

facts.statement: Martilla considers P. andrewsi to be a large form of the genus Peloneustes.
facts.quote: Martilla constituye una forma grande del género Peloneustes

facts.statement: P. portentificus originates from the late Kimmeridgian of England.
facts.quote: Pliosaurus portentificus procede de finales del Kimmeridgiense de Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The Svalbard specimen lived approximately 147 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los restos de la criatura, que vivió hace unos 147 millones de años, son exhibidos en el Museo de Historia Natural de Oslo.

facts.statement: The genus Pliosaurus lived from the Callovian to the Maastrichtian, between 165.3 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Maastrichtian (165.3 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Pliosaurus belongs to the parent group Thalassophonea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Thalassophonea

facts.statement: The genus Pliosaurus belongs to the family Pliosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Pliosauridae

facts.statement: The genus Pliosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: There are 57 recorded fossil occurrences of the genus Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 57
